abilities.description: Builds and aims handheld sun-lenses to signal, light fires, and deflect focused light.
abilities.name: Sun-lens Craft

abilities.description: Improvises shielded cases and hand-driven mechanisms that keep devices working through solar storm surges.
abilities.name: Shielded Case Rigging

characters.arc: Mira begins as a brilliant but rigid technician who trusts only her numbers. Through the crossing she learns to rely on other people's knowledge, adapts her designs to messy reality, and ends by bridging the Concord and the Seedkeepers.
characters.description: A seventeen-year-old apprentice lens-engineer from Westerly Greenhold, small and wiry, with sun-freckled skin, a braid threaded with copper wire, and permanently ink-stained fingers. She grew up repairing mirrored light-wells on the outer canopy and was among the first to notice the rogue satellite's beam scorching her home's terraces.
characters.external_conflict: The Concord refuses to support a Wastes expedition, and the daily satellite sweeps and approaching storm leave her little time.
characters.flaw: Overconfident in her own calculations, she dismisses advice that does not fit her models.
characters.goal: Reach Emberroot Seed Vault and return with seeds and knowledge to rebuild Westerly before the solar storm hits.
characters.internal_conflict: She was raised to trust the Concord's rationing logic, but begins to suspect that protecting the grid alone means abandoning living things, which clashes with the Seed Oath she swore.
characters.motivation: To save the canopy and gardens where she grew up, and the family who tend them, from the satellite's burning beam.
characters.name: Mira Solenne

abilities.description: Identifies, preserves, and revives rare seeds and hardy plants, including those that can grow in salt-damaged soil.
abilities.name: Seed Lore

abilities.description: Reads salt-tolerant plants and marsh growth to find safe ground and clean water.
abilities.name: Wastes Plant Reading

characters.arc: Oren moves from guilty isolation to open leadership, sharing the vault's secrets, trusting younger allies, and rejoining the Seedkeepers on his own terms.
characters.description: A reclusive botanist in his fifties with weathered brown skin, grey-streaked hair, and a patched green coat full of seed pouches. A Seedkeeper once close to the vault's final custodians, he withdrew to Westerly's tallest greenhouse after the Vault Sealing dispute and has kept the vault's old route in his memory and notebooks.
characters.external_conflict: The Concord regards him as a disruptive relic, and the Wastes themselves can overwhelm the route he remembers.
characters.flaw: He avoids people and withholds information out of old guilt, so allies are often left guessing.
characters.goal: Guide Mira to Emberroot Vault and reopen it so thousands of lost species can be restored.
characters.internal_conflict: He fears that reopening the vault will repeat the dispute that tore the Seedkeepers apart and make him responsible once more.
characters.motivation: To honor the Seed Oath and redeem his silence about the vault's location during the old succession dispute.
characters.name: Oren Vael

abilities.description: Sails solar-cell skiffs across salt flats and glass fields, even through mirage storms.
abilities.name: Skiff Piloting

abilities.description: Reads glints, salt crust, and acid pools to find safe routes.
abilities.name: Safe-Path Reading

characters.arc: Kesh moves from guarded bargaining to real partnership, ending as the Tidewrights' ambassador to the Greenholds.
characters.description: A twenty-year-old sail-skiff pilot of the Tidewrights with a sun-cracked grin, salt-bleached hair, and mirrored goggles. She grew up among Rustwake's rusting cranes and learned the safe paths of the Saltglass Wastes from her grandmother.
characters.external_conflict: Her elders demand a reckoning from the Concord before any help is given, and mirage storms threaten each crossing.
characters.flaw: Her distrust of arcology folk makes her sarcastic and quick to test or abandon partners.
characters.goal: Pilot the heroes across the Wastes while securing a promise that the Tidewrights will have a voice in the Greenholds.
characters.internal_conflict: She wants to help the heroes but fears she is serving the same people who shut her ancestors out.
characters.motivation: To win recognition and fair treatment for her people from the arcologies that once closed their gates.
characters.name: Kesh Marrow

abilities.description: Directs power allocation and persuades the Solar Assembly to back his decisions.
abilities.name: Grid Governance

characters.arc: Halden clings to control, but once the seeds prove his plan insufficient he yields, and he finally opens Concord resources to a shared recovery.
characters.description: A tall, silver-haired councilor of the Concord of Light seated at Heliopolis Core, he wears pale solar-weave robes and carries a crystal-lattice cell as a badge of office. A skilled administrator who steered the Greenholds through past shortages, he believes the grid is the only thing keeping humanity alive.
characters.external_conflict: The Seedkeepers and Tidewrights challenge his authority, and Mira's defiance exposes the limits of his plan.
characters.flaw: He treats rationing as an absolute truth and cannot accept risk that might fail visibly.
characters.goal: Divert scarce power into shielding the grid and keep the vault expedition from drawing resources away.
characters.internal_conflict: He privately knows shielding will not heal scorched fields, but admitting it would undermine the order he has built.
characters.motivation: To protect the solar grid and the lives that depend on it from collapse.
characters.name: Councilor Halden Corvane

abilities.description: Moves quickly through maintenance tunnels and canopy scaffolds to deliver messages and supplies.
abilities.name: Tunnel Navigation

abilities.description: Grafts and nurses damaged seedlings back to health.
abilities.name: Grafting

characters.arc: Tamsin learns to channel recklessness into careful stewardship, ending as steward of Westerly's surviving gardens and the first to plant the new seeds.
characters.description: A fifteen-year-old garden runner from Westerly with a gap-toothed smile, scraped knees, and a satchel of grafting tools. Orphaned by the first canopy fires, she lives in the terraces and knows every maintenance tunnel in the city.
characters.external_conflict: The satellite's daily sweep burns the terraces she tends, and Concord wardens try to move her to a safer district.
characters.flaw: She is reckless and hides fear behind jokes, rushing into danger without a plan.
characters.goal: Prove herself useful to Oren and Mira, and keep the garden seedlings alive in their absence.
characters.internal_conflict: She longs to join the expedition but is afraid of being left behind or being a burden.
characters.motivation: To protect the terraces that gave her a family after she lost her own.
characters.name: Tamsin Ryle

relationships.description: Mira Solenne reluctantly partners with Oren Vael, whose botanical knowledge she needs, while his secrecy repeatedly frustrates her engineering certainty.
Councilor Halden Corvane forbids Mira Solenne's expedition and orders her to stay on the canopy, treating her as a risk to the grid he has sworn to protect.
Oren Vael and Councilor Halden Corvane have long clashed over the vault: Oren sees the seeds as essential, while Halden regards them as a dangerous distraction from the grid.
Kesh Marrow guides Mira Solenne across the Wastes, testing her trustworthiness while slowly becoming her friend.
Kesh Marrow resents Councilor Halden Corvane as the face of the Concord that closed its gates to the Tidewrights, and demands he answer for it.
Oren Vael teaches Tamsin Ryle the craft of grafting and seed care, seeing in her a chance to pass on the Seedkeepers' knowledge.
Tamsin Ryle looks up to Mira Solenne like an older sister and secretly helps her slip past the Concord's wardens before the expedition departs.
